key_insight: Artificial flame thickening increases effective flame-scale Karlovitz number and decreases Damköhler number, creating opposing effects on local propagation speed and flame wrinkling in lean hydrogen flames.
engineering_relevance: Accurate coarse-mesh hydrogen combustion predictions require corrections for both local flame propagation and flame area, not wrinkling alone.
method: Analyze over 200 flame-resolved simulations with detailed chemistry and transport in homogeneous isotropic turbulence.
Isolate thickening effects using Ka_f^F = Ka_f√F and Da_f^F = Da_f/F.
Propose an implicit, self-consistent efficiency correction to recover unthickened flame consumption speed.
evidence_signal: Simulations matched in effective Karlovitz and Damköhler numbers collapse across thickening factors until flame thickness approaches integral or geometric length scales.
watch_item: The proposed efficiency correction requires an implicit solution because it feeds back on effective flow–flame parameters; the reported collapse also has a scale-separation limit.
paper_title: A Systematic Assessment of Artificial Flame Thickening for Thermodiffusively Unstable Lean Hydrogen Flames in Homogeneous Isotropic Turbulence
